import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
from sklearn.linear_model import LinearRegression

df = pd.read_csv('/data/worldbank_education_gdp.csv')

# Identify the rows for the relevant indicators
labor_force_row = df[df['Series Name'] == 'Labor force participation rate, total (percentage of total population ages 15+) (modeled ILO estimate)']
primary_enrollment_row = df[df['Series Name'] == 'School enrollment, primary (percentage gross)']
secondary_enrollment_row = df[df['Series Name'] == 'School enrollment, secondary (percentage gross)']
export_growth_row = df[df['Series Name'] == 'Exports of goods and services (annual percentage growth)']

# Extract the values for each year
labor_force_values = labor_force_row.iloc[:, 4:].values[0]
primary_enrollment_values = primary_enrollment_row.iloc[:, 4:].values[0]
secondary_enrollment_values = secondary_enrollment_row.iloc[:, 4:].values[0]
export_growth_values = export_growth_row.iloc[:, 4:].values[0]

# Check for NaN values in export_growth_values
nan_indices = np.isnan(export_growth_values)
print("Indices with NaN values in export_growth_values:", nan_indices)

# Remove rows with NaN values
valid_indices = ~nan_indices
labor_force_values = labor_force_values[valid_indices]
primary_enrollment_values = primary_enrollment_values[valid_indices]
secondary_enrollment_values = secondary_enrollment_values[valid_indices]
export_growth_values = export_growth_values[valid_indices]

# Combine education levels into a single variable
education_levels = np.column_stack((primary_enrollment_values, secondary_enrollment_values))

# Create a linear regression model
model = LinearRegression()
model.fit(education_levels, export_growth_values)

# Get the coefficients
coefficients = model.coef_
intercept = model.intercept_

coefficients, intercept
